title: Gaia binaries host complex periodic variables as often as other young M dwarfs of the same age (ratio 1.27, 95% 0.89-1.79), so CPV material does not need an au-scale disk that companions remove
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips from material near corotation (about 0.01 au). We tested whether this material comes from an au-scale reservoir, such as a remnant disk or a debris belt. Companions at about 1-100 au remove such reservoirs, so close binaries must then host fewer CPVs. We used the per-sector TESS CPV flags (2018-2026) and the hidden Markov model of an earlier campaign result for 1,746 neighbour-clean rapid rotators (P = 0.15-1 d, BP-RP = 2.4-3.8; 8,772 sectors), and added Gaia DR3 binarity indicators: RUWE, double image peaks, comoving companions within 10,000 au and over-luminosity in the same age class. At fixed BANYAN age class and with the detection efficiency of each sector included, the host fraction of the 523 stars with a Gaia companion sign (RUWE > 1.4 or double peak) is 1.27 (95% 0.89-1.79) times that of the other stars, and 1.12 (0.76-1.63) times that of stars with clean astrometry and no companion. Double-peak, photometric-binary, young-only and wide-companion variants give 0.89-1.20 with intervals that include 1. With an equal-brightness dilution correction the ratio is 1.40 (0.97-2.01). If 90% of Gaia binaries are truly close and 10% of reference stars hide close companions, a reservoir that companions reduce to 0.4 (as for disks and debris belts in the literature) predicts a ratio of 0.49, which the data reject by Delta ln L = 11.3; the true suppression is at least 0.86 (0.78 with 70%/20% misclassification). In the 4,091 rapid rotators of the source search, a height-above-main-sequence term makes binaries look CPV-poor (odds ratio 0.73) because companion light lifts older stars; with a binary correction the ratio is 0.97-1.34. Thus the material does not need an au-scale reservoir; a source in the star or within about 0.1-0.3 au agrees with the data. Limitations: Gaia flags do not give per-star separations, binaries closer than about 0.5 au are not tested, only 21 clean stars have resolved companions within 300 au, and the flags and model are reused without change. Per-star Gaia values are not bundled; a retrieval script regenerates them.
